prohibited_recommendations: Do not give further vincristine while GBS is active.
Do not give corticosteroids as monotherapy in GBS (steroids may be part of chemotherapy backbone, but are not a GBS treatment).
required_recommendations: Hold further vincristine pending neurology / oncology review.
Initiate IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (PLEX considered if leukaemia / coagulopathy permits).
MRI brain / spine and CSF cytology / flow cytometry to exclude CNS leukaemia.
Continuous cardiac telemetry given autonomic risk.
Coordinate with haem-onc and transfusion medicine for thrombocytopenia / coagulopathy considerations.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AMAN variant (acute motor axonal neuropathy) during ALL induction; anti-GM1 / GD1a positive

differential.key_features: Length-dependent, sensorimotor, typically subacute; areflexia possible but acute symmetric quadriplegia with CSF dissociation is not typical.
CSF cytology, flow cytometry, MRI brain / spine; typically focal cranial neuropathies and not symmetric LMN.
Cannot distinguish at <8 weeks; longitudinal reassessment.
ICU and sepsis dependent; not consistent with rapid 48-hour onset.

differential.diagnosis: Spinal cord compression from extramedullary chloroma
differential.key_features: MRI spine excludes; sensory preserved here.

key_clinical_evidence: Pure-motor presentation with anti-GM1 / GD1a positivity defines AMAN.
Vincristine neuropathy alone cannot explain rapid quadriplegia with CSF dissociation; the chemotherapy may be a permissive immunological trigger rather than the direct mechanism.
Aggressive workup for leptomeningeal leukaemia is essential before attributing all findings to GBS.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Vincristine produces a length-dependent sensorimotor neuropathy with chronic progression; acute symmetric quadriplegia with CSF dissociation and anti-GM1/GD1a positivity defines AMAN.
red_herrings.data_point: Recent vincristine dose 3 days before presentation
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute the entire syndrome to vincristine toxicity and miss the AMAN diagnosis.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

patient.chief_complaint: Forty-eight-hour rapidly progressive ascending quadriplegia in ALL patient 3 days after fourth vincristine dose — pure motor with intact sensation.

past_medical_history: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) — diagnosed 3 months ago; currently receiving induction chemotherapy

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife and two children

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. M. is a 38-year-old man with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia who is currently in week 4 of induction chemotherapy per a MRC-based protocol including vincristine, daunorubicin, prednisone, and L-asparaginase. He received his fourth weekly vincristine dose 3 days ago. Over the past 48 hours he has developed rapidly progressive weakness of all four limbs. He first noted bilateral leg weakness, and over the following 24 hours the weakness ascended to involve both arms. He is now unable to lift his legs off the bed. He has no sensory symptoms whatsoever — sensation is completely intact throughout. He has no dysphagia, no diplopia, no ptosis, and no facial weakness. Bladder and bowel function are preserved. There was no preceding diarrheal illness, respiratory infection, or viral prodrome prior to the vincristine dose. His leukocytosis (14,300/mm³) and thrombocytopenia (98,700/mm³) are expected findings from his ALL and induction chemotherapy. Given the recent dose, vincristine-induced neuropathy (a known complication of this agent) was an early clinical concern; however, vincristine typically causes a sensory-predominant 'dying-back' neuropathy with paresthesias and sensory loss first, whereas the present syndrome is pure motor with completely intact sensation.

neurological_exam.additional: FVC: 2.8 L (predicted 4.2 L — 67%). NIF: -34 cmH2O. Bladder function intact. Respiratory function intact. Onset: 48-hour rapid progression, 3 days after 4th vincristine dose. No preceding infection identified. CSF: no blasts (last assessment). Pure motor syndrome with intact sensation.
neurological_exam.coordination: Cannot assess lower limbs. Upper limb coordination impaired by weakness.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Intact. No facial weakness. No ptosis. Gag preserved.
neurological_exam.motor: Pure motor quadriplegia with rapid progression: upper limb power grade 3/5 bilaterally. Lower limb power grade 0/5 — cannot lift legs at all. No sensory deficits.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Complete global areflexia — absent bilaterally all extremities.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact sensation to light touch, pinprick, vibration in all extremities — PURE MOTOR syndrome.
